# Brazil Potash Provides Third Quarter 2026 Update as Construction Readiness and Financing Strategy Advance


November 05, 2026 7:00am EST[Download as PDF](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_68804a487ace7405f62c2ff940d5f69f/brazilpotash/news/2026-11-05_Brazil_Potash_Provides_Third_Quarter_2026_Update_68.pdf)


- ***Third quarter milestones included a definitive power agreement that removes approximately $33 million of upfront costs from the construction budget and enactment of new Brazilian legislation, Profert, favorable to the Company***


- ***Front End Engineering Design coverage now spans the full Project, with completion targeted for Q2 2027, a prerequisite for construction debt financing***


- ***The Company continues to make progress on a construction debt financing package with a multilateral bank and Export Credit Agencies***


- ***Cash and cash equivalents of approximately $68.6 million at September 30, 2026; nine-month net loss of approximately $10.5 million***


MANAUS, Brazil, Nov. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Brazil Potash Corp. (“Brazil Potash” or the “Company”) (NYSE American: GRO), a critical mineral exploration and development company advancing the Autazes Potash Project (the “Autazes Project” or “Project”) in Amazonas State, Brazil, today provided an update on the third quarter of 2026 in conjunction with the filing of its condensed interim consolidated financial statements and management’s discussion and analysis for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.


“The Autazes Project continues to be de-risked, and the third quarter demonstrates that,” said Matt Simpson, Chief Executive Officer of Brazil Potash. “Through our strategy to have third parties build major non-core infrastructure to reduce construction financing through BOOT (Build-Own-Operate-Transfer) contracts, we save approximately $33 million of upfront costs for the modular power plant with our Gera Center agreement. The Brazilian government’s new Profert legislation has potential financial benefits for the Project that we continue to review. A challenge to our licenses was also rejected by the courts during the quarter. Looking ahead, we continue to progress discussions on a construction financing package.”


**Third Quarter Highlights**


- **Power:** Signed a definitive 28-year build-own-operate agreement with Gera Center, under which Gera Center will fund, own and operate a 20 MW modular power plant. The plant is expected to provide power needed for construction and then serve as backup power for the mine. The Company expects the arrangement to take approximately $33 million out of upfront construction spending and to save approximately $10 million over the life of the contract.


- **Engineering and Project Site Developments:** Front-end engineering design (“FEED”) now covers the full Project, including the mine shaft and underground development scope awarded in June to WSP UK Ltd., supported by Redpath Deilmann Mining Inc. as subconsultant, with completion targeted for Q2 2027. On-site training programs began, geotechnical drilling arrangements advanced, and the Company continued third-party construction debt diligence.


- **Government Support:** Brazil signed “Profert”, legislation aimed to encourage domestic fertilizer production, into law. Together with the Project’s existing Manaus Free Trade Zone (“SUFRAMA”) tax benefit, Profert offers at least two potential benefits for the Project:


- Lower construction costs: The Company is in the process of analyzing the legislation to assess the potential benefit to the Project. It estimates the two programs could exempt tens of millions in federal taxes and import duties on the Project’s expected US$2.5 billion initial capital cost. Potential future developments in how the government administers the new legislation as well as developments with the Project may also affect the benefit to the Project
- A new source of construction financing: Brazil’s national development bank (“BNDES”) is now authorized to finance new domestic fertilizer production. On August 26, the government announced R$4 billion in additional BNDES-administered financing and working-capital support for the fertilizer sector. This funding could be at favorable interest rates and other terms.


- **Construction Licenses Upheld.** In August, Brazil’s Supreme Federal Court rejected an appeal of recent decisions of the Federal Regional Court of the First Region in support of the Company, leaving in place all 21 licenses required for construction of the Project (“Construction Licenses”) including the mine, processing plant, port and supporting infrastructure. This preserved prior rulings upholding the Project’s Indigenous consultation process. In September 2023, 34 of 36 Mura villages participated and over 90% of participating villagers voted to support the Project.


**Construction and Financing Update**


All 21 Construction Licenses, including those for the processing plant and port, are in place, and recent court decisions have preserved prior rulings upholding those licenses and the Indigenous consultation process as described above.


Brazil Potash continues to pursue its strategy of reducing the capital it must raise before production by having specialized partners fund, build and operate major infrastructure under build-own-operate and build-own-operate-transfer (“BOOT”) agreements. In addition to the Gera Center agreement announced during the quarter, the Company is in discussions with other third parties on additional infrastructure packages.


Since quarter-end, the Company reported initial results from AI-powered X-ray Transmission (XRT) sorting testwork that suggest potential to increase production and/or extend mine life. Due to the small sample tested, the results are indicative and cannot yet be regarded as representative of full-scale mine production. The Company intends to perform additional testwork and further engineering and economic analysis to consider implementation at the Project


**Financial Position**


As of September 30, 2026, Brazil Potash had cash and cash equivalents of approximately $68.6 million and working capital of approximately $67.3 million, compared with cash and cash equivalents of approximately $27.8 million at December 31, 2025, and approximately $75.7 million at June 30, 2026. The increase since year-end was due primarily to net proceeds of approximately $59.0 million from the public offering that closed on May 4, 2026. Current liabilities were approximately $1.9 million, and the Company had no debt.


For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, net cash used in operating activities was approximately $7.3 million and net cash used in investing activities, primarily exploration and evaluation spending, was approximately $10.6 million. Net loss for the period was approximately $10.5 million, compared with approximately $45.2 million a year earlier, primarily due to lower share-based compensation and higher finance income. For the third quarter, operating loss was approximately $2.8 million and net loss was approximately $1.2 million.


The Company believes its cash on hand is sufficient to cover its planned activities for 2027 which includes making a final investment decision to start construction subject to raising prerequisite funding. The Company continues discussions on a financing package for the Project construction, including debt and equity components.


**Corporate Updates**


The Company appointed Sean Keating as Chief Legal Officer effective October 1, 2026.


Effective on or about Monday, November 9th, the Company will be changing the address of its head office to 365 Bay St. Ste 800, Toronto, ON M5H 2V1.


**Share Count and Capital Structure**


As of filing, Brazil Potash had 62,126,240 common shares issued and outstanding, compared with 61,946,215 at June 30, 2026, with the increase reflecting the settlement of restricted share units. The Company’s 22,850,000 outstanding pre-funded warrants, do not expire and carry no voting rights, remain unexercised and are not included in the common share count until exercised. The Company has not used its at-the-market equity distribution agreement, which provides for sales of up to $125 million, since establishing it in April 2026, and has not sold any shares under its equity line of credit in 2026.


**Market Backdrop**


During the quarter, multiple multilateral development banks and international financial institutions, including the Inter-American Development Bank Group and the World Bank Group, issued a joint statement on strengthening fertilizer supply chains that called for increased financing across fertilizer production, processing, storage, transportation and other critical infrastructure. This press release can be accessed using this link: https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/statement/2026/08/31/joint-statement-by-the-multilateral-development-banks-and-international-financial


Brazil Potash remains focused on advancing construction financing and moving the Autazes Project toward construction.


Brazil Potash’s condensed interim consolidated financial statements and management’s discussion and analysis for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 are available on SEC.gov and at ir.brazilpotash.com.


**About Brazil Potash**


Brazil Potash (NYSE American: GRO) (www.brazilpotash.com), through its subsidiary Potássio do Brasil, is developing the Autazes Project to supply potash to one of the world's largest agricultural exporters. Brazil is critical for global food security, with among the highest amounts of fresh water and arable land and an ideal climate for year-round crop growth, yet the country imported approximately 96% of the potash it consumed in 2025 despite hosting what is anticipated to be one of the world's largest undeveloped potash basins. The potash produced will be transported primarily using low-cost river barges on an inland river system in partnership with Amaggi (www.amaggi.com.br), one of Brazil's largest farmers and logistical operators of agricultural products.
